Case studies

01Microsoft · Copilot Studio2025–2026

7 shipped product decisions

as a result of research to answer: how do enterprises know an AI agent is ready to ship?

7 decisions
shipped in the product, plus the design of two new evaluation surfaces

My role: Co-led the discovery interviews; led the synthesis, the structure study and the readouts.

01Problem
  • Agents were entering business-critical work faster than teams could check them.
02Method
  • 35 interviews across two studies, users and non-users.
  • Competitive IA review; 170+ jobs to be done.
03Insight
  • "What broke?" belongs to developers; "Is this acceptable?" to QA and experts.
  • Release decisions ran on consensus, not metrics.
04Impact
  • 7 shipped decisions, including separate Test and Evaluate surfaces and pass/fail ship signals instead of percentage scores.
  • Informed a new evaluation hub and the evaluation tab in the agent operations area.
  • Criteria adopted by product, security and governance.
Built from the research

Evaluations JTBD Simulator

172 jobs to be done across 11 themes and 5 lifecycle stages. PMs and designers pick a stage and a theme to see what builders need there, or combine themes to find the jobs that span several, the high-leverage bets to prioritize. Used by PMs and designers in design decisions.

Try the live simulator ↗
02Meta · Instagram Shops2020–2023

A redesigned product page and a dropped feature

as a result of research to answer: which details make an Instagram shopper buy?

9 of 17
tested variables drove conversion. Price guarantee was not one of them.

My role: Lead researcher. Designed and ran the interviews and the 9,000-person choice study.

01Problem
  • One layout for every category; engineering needed variables to model.
02Method
  • 12 in-depth interviews.
  • Discrete choice, n=9,000: 17 variables, 90 levels.
03Insight
  • 3 fashion and 6 cross-category variables drive conversion.
  • Price guarantee did no better than the rest.
04Impact
  • Variables used to train the model behind a personalized product page.
  • Price guarantee feature dropped.
03Meta · Express Wi-Fi2020–2023

+36% weekly registrations

as a result of research to answer: why was free Wi-Fi in Delhi missing its targets?

+36%
weekly registrations after the fixes

My role: Led the connectivity insights work. Designed and ran the Delhi interviews and combined them with platform and access point data.

01Problem
  • Usage far below forecast; a city partnership at stake.
02Method
  • In-depth interviews.
  • Usage data by gender; access point mapping.
03Insight
  • Sign-up asked for private ID and was hard on feature phones.
  • Hotspots were on the street, where women were less likely to go.
04Impact
  • Simpler, icon-led sign-up and Sign in with Facebook; access points moved toward homes.
  • Weekly registrations +36%.
04SodaStream · PepsiCo2017–2020

Patented hardware and 2 new factories

as a result of research to answer: why were customers dropping off a refill-driven business?

2 factories
built to produce the redesigned cylinder system

My role: Global Head of User & Consumer Insight. Led the ethnography within the global research program.

01Problem
  • High churn; earlier analysis had not found the cause.
02Method
  • In-home ethnography in a global qual and quant program.
03Insight
  • People want water cold: 2–3 bottles chilling, but only 1 shipped.
  • Empty cylinders were forgotten in car trunks.
04Impact
  • Patented quick-connect cylinder and valve, a new machine, 2 new factories.
  • Home delivery extended to more markets.

Research ops I built

Tools and processes that make research faster to run and easier to reuse.

★ UserTesting ILLUMI Award 2026

AI-first study automation

Problem: setting up unmoderated studies by hand was slow and error-prone.

  1. Brief
  2. Screener logic
  3. Sample size
  4. Build & launch
  5. Transcripts back
  • A conversational agent sets up a full UserTesting study from a short brief.
  • An MCP server connects to the UserTesting API; browser automation covers the rest.

Impact: Microsoft named winner of UserTesting's 2026 Innovation Catalyst Award; individual ILLUMI Award.

Demo, 2:35

Framework + live scorer

Human Grade Benchmark Kit

Problem: "consumer-grade" was a goal with no definition.

  • 25 rules from teardowns of 30 consumer apps and 15 creation tools, including 7 neuroinclusion rules.
  • A plugin walks a product in a real browser, screenshots each step and scores it.
  • Piloted on a live enterprise product.
Hackathon 2026

Human Value Add Assessor

Problem: teams need a fair way to show what a person adds beyond what AI produces.

Walkthrough (1:53): upload → artifact type → rules → score with cited evidence.

  • Upload a deck, doc, sheet or page. One model writes the brief, a second makes a blind AI version, a third compares.
  • 98-attribute rubric in 8 categories.
  • Every score needs cited evidence; the creator's identity is hidden.
Shared skills

10 AI research skills

Reusable skills I wrote for the team library: run-usability-test, recruit-personas, think-aloud-test, usability-synthesis, assess-product-live, neuroinclusion-eval and more.

Talks, workshops and training

Talks, workshops and training I have led.

Talk · IIEX West 2026 · San Francisco · October 2026

From Hype to Human

A New Horizon for AI and Business. Co-presented with Julius Colwyn of Space Doctors. When we scale old business assumptions with AI, value starts to distort. The opportunity is to find the new value AI opens up, and put human value at the center of how business works.

AssumptionScaled with AIWhat if…
Everyone needs a clearly defined role.Roles blur: engineers design, designers code. Output rises, quality stagnates.Roles were defined around judgement and accountability, with shared quality standards?
Senior employees will mentor juniors.As AI takes junior work, there is less reason to delegate and teach.Juniors were tasked with reimagining how AI brings new value?
Removing human effort improves the experience.AI removes tedium, but also agency, mastery and participation.Products told unwanted effort apart from effort people value?
Three tensions to resolve
Output vs. OutcomeMeasure success by human value, not volume.
Product vs. ProcessTreat divergent, distinctive approaches as the source of value.
Scale vs. SkillKeep the talent pipeline that delivers on the technology.
“Prioritizing speed drives convergence. The new value comes from divergence.”
Volume → Human value
System-defined → Self-defined productivity
Grind → Experience

Future of the product, with its leaders

Designed and co-facilitated for product, engineering, design, data science and marketing leads. Pre-work tracks, structured debate, persona stress tests and a "what must be true" gap analysis, aimed at 3–5 priorities with named owners.

3 days
Cross-disciplinary design sprint
Design sprint · 2026

From research to concepts

In person, with design, product and engineering. I led the cultural and vision strand. Output: a North Star, guiding metaphors, and design concepts with validation plans.

Training I run
  • Introducing foresight: horizon scanning, trend clustering and futures wheels for product teams.
  • How to use research to 10x product impact: a talk for product teams on bringing researchers in early and acting on findings.
  • STEEP trend scanning: a recurring program for the product organization, with at least three independent sources per trend.
Writing
Essay · 2026

The Convergence Trap

Default AI use pulls teams toward the same average answers. I argue for using AI heavily where work converges and holding it back where ideas need to diverge.

Editorial · 2026

Neuroinclusion in enterprise AI

At least 1 in 5 employees is neurodivergent and about a third never disclose it, so opt-in modes miss most of them. Output: an 8-principle audit used in product assessments.
